appraisal_events.evidence: Hosts anxiously await word that her carriage has been seen, and once she appears at their modest gathering "reprenait tout son lustre aux yeux des maîtres de maison," who are overjoyed to see her name printed "en tête" in the society column of Le Gaulois.
appraisal_events.explanation: The dowager marquise's mere attendance at minor local gatherings is shown conferring enormous, publicly registered prestige on her hosts, confirming her own towering local standing.

appraisal_events.evidence: "l'impolitesse de sa belle-fille née Legrandin qui, par son arrogance, relevait la bonhomie un peu fade de la belle-mère."
appraisal_events.explanation: The hosts' retrospective judgment contrasts the daughter-in-law's arrogant rudeness with the dowager's good-natured plainness, comparatively favoring the mother-in-law.

status_effects.explanation: Her presence is anxiously courted and publicly registered (society-column mention, hosts' relief and pride), a clear witnessed elevation of standing.
Her plain good nature is favorably set off by contrast with her daughter-in-law's arrogance in the hosts' recollection.
She is judged impolite and arrogant by comparison with her mother-in-law in the same recollection.
